Hi all — quick technical options based on Camila's note and SleepWell asks. High level: we can produce event-level exports in both CSV (human-inspectable) and Parquet (efficient, columnar) formats. Below is a minimal schema and delivery/chain-of-custody options.

Minimal CSV schema (column names):
- event_ts_utc (ISO8601 with milliseconds, e.g. 2027-11-01T22:34:12.123Z)
- actor_id_hashed (sha256 hex)
- actor_role (user | service | api-key)
- resource_id (model_request_id)
- action_type (invoke | read | download | modify)
- model_version
- region
- request_trace_id (UUID)
- response_size_bytes
- note (optional short string)

Hashing & identity:
- We can apply sha256 with either a Redwood ephemeral salt or a customer-provided salt. If SleepWell provides the salt under NDA, we can use that so hashes are reversible by you only. We do NOT include raw PII in exports unless explicitly requested and contractually approved.

Residency & delivery: 
- Exports can be generated in-region and delivered to an EU-hosted S3 bucket if you require EU residency.
- Delivery options: presigned S3 link (HTTPS, 24–72h expiry), TLS SFTP push to your endpoint, or encrypted zip with per-file AES-256 + shared key.

Retention & proof: 
- We support snapshot exports (ad-hoc for a given range) and scheduled daily deltas. Retention policy enforcement is configured per-customer: defaults are 30/90/365 days; we can configure longer (e.g., 7 years) with an enterprise retention addendum and note the storage implications.
- For chain-of-custody we can provide: signed manifest (HMAC-SHA256) listing files + sizes + checksums, and a timestamped delivery record. We can also provide a signed statement from our security team for audit purposes.

Sample filename convention: sleepwell_who_viewed_when_20271101_20271102_UTC.csv

I'll generate a 48-hour sample (with hashed actor ids and UTC timestamps) and upload it via a presigned S3 link by tomorrow morning. Let me know if you want raw request payloads included; that increases sensitivity and will require contract-level approvals.

-Karthik

Hi team — quick note on recommended contract language and risks to surface: 

1) Evidence delivery SLA: suggest 5 business days for ad-hoc snapshot exports in the Master Services Agreement, with an option for shorter SLAs as part of an enterprise addendum.
2) Retention and certification: include a retention appendix that enumerates retention windows per data class (audit logs vs raw input artifacts). For PII-derived artifacts requiring 7-year retention, include customer-paid storage addendum and technical controls (region-scoped storage + KMS key residency).
3) Chain-of-custody: require that Redwood provide a signed manifest (HMAC) and checksums for exported files; include sample language that Redwood will provide attestations of export generation time and delivery method.
4) Data residency warranty: we can warrant that exports generated for EU-resident data will be produced and delivered from EU-hosted infrastructure; avoid a broad cross-border warranty unless we coordinate with infra/ops.
